title: Window
description: Query exact HWND/process/physical bounds, focus or move a verified window, and enumerate/switch/move windows by virtual desktop GUID. Unsupported COM builds fail explicitly; no message injection or hidden-window screenshot.
name: Window

title: ControlStatus
description: Get desktop control owner, enabled state, gate policy, configured idle timeout and remaining user idle wait in seconds. AI control has no time limit: it lasts until the user takes over or release=true hands the desktop back, so release when the desktop work is done or before waiting on the user. Settings are read-only and changes require a server restart.
name: ControlStatus

title: App
description: Open/start/launch applications and manage windows. Keywords: open, start, launch, program, application, window, foreground, focus, resize. Four modes: 'launch' (opens an application by Start Menu name), 'launch_executable' (strictly launches one executable path with separated argv and optional cwd), 'resize' (adjusts a named or active window), and 'switch' (brings a specific window into focus). Prefer background execution when supported. If launching an application is known to take focus or disrupt the user, obtain permission first, reusing existing authorization. Relaxed policy does not gate launch modes; this guidance is not server-enforced approval.
name: App

title: Snapshot
description: Take a screenshot and inspect the screen. Keywords: screenshot, screen capture, see screen, observe, look, inspect, UI elements, what's on screen. Captures complete desktop state including: system language, focused/opened windows, interactive elements (buttons, text fields, links, menus with coordinates), and scrollable areas. Set use_vision=True to include screenshot with cursor highlight. Set use_annotation=False to get a clean screenshot without bounding box overlays on UI elements (default: True, draws colored rectangles around detected elements). Set use_ui_tree=False for a faster screenshot-only snapshot when you do not need interactive or scrollable element extraction. Set width_reference_line/height_reference_line to overlay a grid for better spatial reasoning (make sure vision is enabled to use it). Set use_dom=True for browser content to get web page elements instead of browser UI. Set display=[0] or display=[0,1] using zero-based active Windows display indices; omit it to keep the default full-desktop behavior. Set region=[left, top, right, bottom] in virtual-desktop pixel coordinates to capture and inspect only that rectangle instead of the whole screen/display — useful when you already know which area matters and want to save tokens; region takes precedence over display when both are given, and an invalid or out-of-bounds region raises an error rather than silently capturing something else. Set save_path to an absolute file path (or an existing directory for a timestamped name) to also write the returned screenshot as a PNG file; this turns on use_vision and the saved path is reported in the response. Existing files are never overwritten. Always call this first to understand the current desktop state before taking actions.
name: Snapshot

title: Screenshot
description: Captures a fast screenshot-first desktop snapshot with cursor position, desktop/window summaries, and an image. This path skips UI tree extraction for speed. Use Snapshot when you need interactive element ids, scrollable regions, or browser DOM extraction. Set display=[0] or display=[0,1] using zero-based active Windows display indices to capture only those monitors. Set region=[left, top, right, bottom] in virtual-desktop pixel coordinates to capture only that rectangle instead of the whole screen/display — useful when you already know which area matters and want to save tokens; region takes precedence over display when both are given, and an invalid or out-of-bounds region raises an error rather than silently capturing something else. Set save_path to an absolute file path (or an existing directory for a timestamped name) to also write the returned image as a PNG file (same pixels as the returned image); the saved path is reported in the response and existing files are never overwritten. Note: the returned image may be downscaled for efficiency; when it is, multiply image coordinates by the ratio of original size to displayed size to get the actual screen coordinates for mouse actions (Click, Move, etc.).
name: Screenshot

title: Click
description: Performs mouse clicks at specified coordinates [x, y] or passing a UI element's label/id. Supports button types: 'left' for selection/activation, 'right' for context menus, 'middle'. Supports clicks: 0=hover only (no click), 1=single click (select/focus), 2=double click (open/activate). Provide either loc or label.
name: Click

title: Type
description: Types text at specified coordinates [x, y] or passing a UI element's label/id. Set clear=True to clear existing text first (Home, Shift+End, Backspace; never Ctrl+A, which many apps treat as 'mark every record'), False to append. The answer says how the field was cleared and what it reads back when the field exposes its text, and warns when focus moved away while typing (e.g. a message box took the keystrokes). Set press_enter=True to submit after typing. Set caret_position to 'start' or 'end' to type at the beginning or end of the field (Home/End; Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End when the clicked field is a document or a native multi-line edit box, so the whole text rather than the clicked line), or 'idle' (default) to type where the click put the caret. Provide either loc or label. clear and press_enter accept only true or false. An empty text types nothing, so combine it with clear=True to just empty a field.
name: Type

title: Scroll
description: Scrolls at coordinates [x, y], a UI element's label/id, or current mouse position if loc=None. Type: vertical (default) or horizontal. Direction: up/down for vertical, left/right for horizontal. wheel_times controls amount (1 wheel ≈ 3-5 lines). Use for navigating long content, lists, and web pages.
name: Scroll

title: Move
description: Moves mouse cursor to coordinates [x, y] or passing a UI element's label/id. Set drag=True to perform a drag-and-drop operation from the current mouse position to the target coordinates, or provide from_loc=[x, y] to make the drag explicit-start and atomic in one tool call. Optional duration controls bounded intermediate movement. Default (drag=False) is a simple cursor move (hover). Drag uses synthesized mouse input, which XAML shell surfaces such as Start menu tiles and pinned taskbar buttons ignore: there the drag does nothing even though the call succeeds, so use their context-menu commands (for example Move to front) instead and check the result with a Screenshot. Provide either loc or label.
name: Move

title: Shortcut
description: Executes keyboard shortcuts using key combinations separated by +. Examples: "ctrl+c" (copy), "ctrl+v" (paste), "alt+tab" (switch apps), "win+r" (Run dialog), "win" (Start menu), "ctrl+shift+esc" (Task Manager). Use for quick actions and system commands.
name: Shortcut

title: Wait
description: Pauses execution for specified duration in seconds. Use when waiting for: applications to launch/load, UI animations to complete, page content to render, dialogs to appear, or between rapid actions. Helps ensure UI is ready before next interaction.
name: Wait

title: MultiSelect
description: Selects multiple items such as files, folders, or checkboxes if press_ctrl=True, or performs multiple clicks if False. Pass locs (list of coordinates) or labels (list of UI element labels/ids).
name: MultiSelect

title: MultiEdit
description: Enters text into multiple input fields at specified coordinates locs=[[x,y,text], ...] or using labels=[[label,text], ...]. Provide either locs or labels.
name: MultiEdit

title: Clipboard
description: Copy/paste clipboard operations. Keywords: copy, paste, cut, clipboard, text transfer. Use mode="get" to read current clipboard content, mode="set" to set clipboard text. This is the real Windows clipboard; set overwrites shared contents. Avoid using it merely to pass data between tools and coordinate known interference with the user.
name: Clipboard
